[22 July 2026, 3-4 — Himaya Perumal]. [2 July 2026, 4 — Himaya Perumal].
*   **Integration of AI Components:** Himaya successfully integrated the AI part of the system, confirming, "Yes, yes, yes, yes" when asked if she had done so. [22 July 2026, 7 — Himaya Perumal].

She also acknowledged that caching solves problems related to latency and recompute. [28 July 2026, 7-8 — Himaya Perumal; 31 July 2026, 11-12 — Himaya Perumal].
*   **Understanding of User-Scoped Memory:** Himaya grasped the concept of user-scoped memory in a multi-agent system, explaining that conversations would be tied to a user ID and stored as metadata, ensuring privacy and personalized retrieval. [28 July 2026, 14-15 — Himaya Perumal].
*   **Ability to Articulate Agent Roles:** Himaya could describe the roles of the agents she designed, including a manager, mentor evaluation performance, and team agents. [28 July 2026, 8-9 — Himaya Perumal].

**Knowledge Gaps:**

*   **Deep Understanding of Caching Implementation:** While Himaya understood the *purpose* of caching, her initial implementation was flawed. Siddharth noted, "instead of you dashing your caching the, you know, the documents, you have cached the user input. Like, I'm not sure why you have done that user input anyway, we need to embed it, so that is no point in caching it." [22 July 2026, 2-3 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He further instructed her to "figure out, like, understand how taxes are actually built, how are they stored, look to look into embedding caches." [22 July 2026, 2-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Distinguishing Caching Types (KV Cache vs. Embedding Cache):** Himaya initially confused KV caching (hardware level) with embedding caching, stating, "because the LLM was doing the KV caching, no, so, so I gave it for the user input, and that was my mistake." Siddharth clarified that "KV cache is different. KV cache doesn't have to do anything. KV cache is a is at the hardware level, hardware level, it's not at the this level." [22 July 2026, 2-3 — Himaya Perumal; 30 July 2026, 2-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Understanding of Scaling:** Himaya struggled to explain how caching contributes to scaling, with Siddharth correcting her: "Embedding cash only saves the cost, it doesn't help you scale. So you understand what scaling actually means." [28 July 2026, 8-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Critical Evaluation of Metadata Filtering for Cost:** Himaya incorrectly believed metadata filtering would reduce token cost, stating, "it will what it will reduce the token size." Siddharth explicitly corrected this, "Metadata filtering does nothing to cost. It has nothing to do with cost." [28 July 2026, 7-8 — Siddharth Saminathan].
*   **Vagueness in Agent Capabilities (Team Intelligence Agent):** Siddharth found Himaya's description of the "team intelligence agent" to be "a bit vague," indicating a need for more concrete and first-principles thinking about what "intelligence" truly means in this context. [17 August 2026, 1-2 — Siddharth Saminathan].
